what_happened: The task record names one hard-stop cause for 'CI / Build and Test' (the closureList ambiguity). Local measurement found a SECOND, masked failure: 'lake exe lint-style' exits 1 with 4 'space before a semicolon' findings in FormalSystem/Metalogic/Expressiveness/SeparationZ/NormalForm.lean:383,390,413,420 (introduced 2026-11-06, commit 7e00fe171). That CI step is currently SKIPPED because the 'Compile BimodalToolsTest' hard stop precedes it, so fixing the ambiguity alone leaves the job red via the aggregating 'Report results' gate.

docs/development/LEAN_STYLE_GUIDE.md section 5 mandates a deprecated alias retaining the old name on any rename. Measured via lean_run_code that a '@[deprecated] abbrev' keeping the old name still produces 'Ambiguous term' under two opens, so following section 5 literally on a closureList rename would leave CI red. The rename recommendation must waive the alias explicitly.

gh is authenticated here, so 'gh run view <id> --json jobs' gave a per-step pass/fail map of the real CI run instead of inferring from workflow YAML. That is what established the ambiguity as the SOLE hard stop and identified exactly which three steps are skipped behind it -- the lead that found the masked lint-style failure.

A second run of scripts/check-evidence-probes.sh reported 'FAIL (untracked: ...)' for 19 consecutive wired probes, exiting 1. Spurious: every one of the 19 is verifiably tracked (git ls-files --error-unmatch succeeds for all 19; git status --untracked-files=all lists only the two history-morphism-saturation-audit files), and an earlier sweep PASSed 12 of the same 19. The all-pass-then-all-fail-from-one-point signature is a transient in the script's own 'git ls-files' subprocess, not a property of the tree. Resolved by re-testing trackedness directly and elaborating the 7 probes neither sweep reached: 67 of 67 PASS. A reader who took the 19 FAILs at face value would have filed a large, entirely fictitious version-control repair.

The Bash tool force-backgrounds any call exceeding 180s regardless of the timeout parameter passed, so the bounded single-call waiter idiom from context/project/lean4/operations/long-builds.md could not be completed inside one call for the ~10-minute evidence-probe sweep. Worked around by reading the detached log and the harness completion notification. Worth noting for the long-builds contract: the documented 600000ms per-call ceiling is not what this harness actually enforces.
